inputs.share_count_basis: 118,191,578 issued less 9,228,390 treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin). No dilutive potential shares (FY2026 AR EPS note). Held flat; the May-2026 ToSTNeT-3 buyback (2,644,800 shares) is already in the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-06-30: short-term borrowings 255,485 + CP 62,000 + current bonds 12,700 + bonds 42,300 + LT borrowings 147,908 = 520,393 interest-bearing debt (company definition), plus finance lease liabilities 17,692 (FY2026 year-end, latest disclosed; treated as debt), less cash and deposits 158,907. The cash includes ~95bn drawn in Q1 FY2027 to pre-fund CalPortland's $712M purchase of Vulcan Materials' California ready-mix assets (agreed 2025-10-28, not yet consolidated at 2026-06-30: goodwill 430m, PP&E +13bn only). The model values the ORGANIC business and keeps that cash in the bridge; the acquired flows and the cash leaving are excluded together, which is value-neutral if the assets were bought at fair value and mildly generous if 1.36x sales for ready-mix was full.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income 1,179m is NOT stripped: the company is a net borrower (net debt 2.6x EBITDA), so the owner-FCF interest rule (strip only when net cash is material) does not apply.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in any FY2018-FY2026 filing (J-GAAP cement producer; cash-settled director remuneration only). SBC-zero market: rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 purchase of treasury shares 27m; FY2025 15,177m; a 10.0bn FCSR buyback executed 2026-05-13 (in Q1 FY2027 financing). Flat count is funded by a real repurchase programme (33%+ TSR ratio policy), not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. 10y JGB ~1.8% + beta ~0.95 x 6.0% JPY ERP = cost of equity ~7.5%. The company funds roughly half its enterprise value with debt at ~1.5% pre-tax (FY2026 interest 6.0bn on ~400bn), so a textbook WACC would be ~4.5-5%; the house deliberately discounts owner FCF at the equity-like 7.5% with no debt-shield credit, because the 2.6x ND/EBITDA leverage on a cyclical is itself the reason not to lower the rate. Same 7.5% in all three scenarios: cyclicality, energy-cost and Philippines/US risks are charged in the scenario flows and the weights, not in the rate (risk charged once). Below the ~9% house reference for JPY keiretsu auto suppliers because this is a domestic oligopoly with long-lived assets, an A+/A credit (JCR/R&I) and a counter-cyclical waste-disposal segment, not an auto-cycle Tier-1.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt. J-GAAP: operating leases are expensed inside operating profit already; the 17,692m finance-lease liability (FY2026 year-end) is added to net debt and its renewal runs through the capex % line. No lease principal deducted from the flows, so no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI ~1.4-1.5bn/yr of a 27-59bn profit, 4.6% of net assets); the 32,441m NCI book value at 2026-06-30 is deducted once in the equity bridge. Not folded into the tax rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Cement producer, J-GAAP, JPY statements and JPY quote. SBC is zero so house and street coincide (band_position null). Risk is charged in the flows: margins ramp DOWN from the FY2025-26 cycle high (16.2% EBITDA after cumulative ~7,000 yen/t domestic price revisions) toward a mid-cycle 14.5% (9-year range 8.5%-16.2%, mean ~13.2%), and capex steps down from the 26 Medium-Term Plan peak (11.2% of revenue FY2026, 9.5% five-year mean) toward 8.5% against D&A of ~8%. Cash tax 30% on EBIT throughout (statutory ~30.6%; FY2026 cash taxes 14.7bn were 20% of EBIT thanks to loss carry-forwards and overseas rates, not a repeatable base). Working capital capture -10% of the revenue change: receivables + inventory (~334bn) far exceed trade payables (~92bn). Revenue base is FY2026 organic (898.4bn); the FY2027 guide of 1,027bn (+14.3%) includes the Vulcan ready-mix assets that the Q1 FY2027 cash build pre-funds, so the organic year-1 growth is set at 3% (Q1 FY2027 ran +5.1% organic; domestic volumes -6.8% offset by pricing and exports; US pricing up). FY2027 OP guidance of 76bn on an organic ~925bn base implies ~8.2% OP / ~16% EBITDA, which is year-1 base. Equity bridge: + investment securities 152.6bn (AFS cross-shareholdings at fair value plus 85bn equity-method affiliates whose income sits outside EBITDA) less 14.7bn deferred tax on the 47.3bn pre-tax unrealised AFS gain; - NCI 32.4bn. Retirement benefit asset 69.8bn and land 167.6bn at book are NOT added (not realisable without changing the business). FINDING: at these driver paths the bear case produces equity at or near the zero floor -- a 2.6x-levered, sub-WACC-ROIC (NOPAT ~52bn on ~1.1tn invested capital = ~4.8%) business has little DCF cushion in a repeat of the FY2023 energy shock. The market price (P/B ~0.7, EV/EBITDA ~5.8x) is paying for asset value and the Palliser activist thesis (CalPortland sale/IPO at ~444bn), not for owner cash flow; that re-rating case is a memo, not the house value.
inputs.fy2022_revenue_break_note: FY2022 revenue fell 18% (863.9bn -> 708.2bn) while gross profit fell 8%; the parser flagged a probable revenue-recognition change (ASBJ Standard 29, mandatory from FY2022 for March year-ends, nets agency/consignment sales). Historical CAGRs are computed on 3- and 5-year windows that both start after or at FY2021; the 5-year revenue CAGR spans the break and is therefore understated by the presentation change.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities at 2026-06-30 (AFS cross-shareholdings at fair value + equity-method affiliates), net of 30% deferred tax on unrealised AFS gains
equity_bridge.note: 152,613m balance sheet (Q1 FY2027 tanshin) less 14,661m tax on the 47,293m pre-tax gain behind the 32,632m net valuation difference. Matching-asset rule: dividend and equity-method income are below operating profit and excluded from EBITDA, so the source assets enter the bridge.
Flows are consolidated; NCI charged once, here.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: domestic cement demand is in structural decline (-5 to -6%/yr volume) offset by price revisions and exports; organic revenue has compounded ~0.8%/yr over five years and ~3.5%/yr over the price-revision window. 1.5% is the midpoint, used as the year-3/4 base growth before fading to a 1.0% terminal.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 7.6% exceeds revenue 0.8% and EPS -10.1% by far more than 30%: book value growth is driven by FX translation (yen weakness on CalPortland), AFS valuation gains and retained earnings, not by operating growth. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth driver.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (SBC 0; interest income not stripped on a net-debt balance sheet). 3-yr EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined because the FY2023 base year was negative (-283.68 EPS, -63.7bn FCF: coal-price shock). FCF is extremely volatile: FY2018-FY2026 reported FCF 55.1, 32.8, 24.5, 51.7, 3.9, -63.7, 53.4, 33.9, 13.2bn, mean ~22.8bn (33.6bn excluding FY2023), because capex (6-11% of revenue) has run ~1.7pp of revenue above D&A on average. The component build, not a trailing CAGR, drives the projection.

base.narrative: Organic business ex-Vulcan. Year-1 ties to FY2027 OP guidance (76bn on an organic ~925bn base). EBITDA margin fades from the price-revision cycle high to a 14.5% mid-cycle; capex steps down from the Medium-Term-Plan peak to 8.5% vs D&A 8.0%. Cap 13x FCF (cyclical) binds over Gordon at 7.5%/1.0%.

bull.narrative: Pricing discipline holds (domestic cement OP margin reaches the 10%+ target), energy costs stay benign, US infrastructure/LA-2028/data-centre demand lifts CalPortland volumes, and growth capex normalises to ~8% once the plan-period projects complete.

bear.narrative: A coal/energy and freight shock in year 2 (Middle East escalation) compresses EBITDA toward the FY2023 trough while price pass-through lags; domestic volumes keep falling 5-6%/yr with pricing unable to offset; US housing stays soft; GX-ETS carbon costs and decarbonisation capex keep investment at 9-10% of revenue. Margins only partially recover to 13%.

scenario_narratives.base: The organic business earns a mid-cycle 14.5% EBITDA margin on revenue growing ~1-1.5%: domestic volumes decline 4-6% a year but the oligopoly keeps passing through costs (cumulative ~7,000 yen/t since FY2023) and blended-cement exports keep plants loaded; CalPortland grows with US infrastructure spending; the Environmental and Mineral Resources segments grow modestly. Capex falls back from the 26 Medium-Term Plan peak (101bn FY2026) toward ~8.5% of revenue, still above D&A to fund decarbonisation. Owner FCF recovers from 13bn (FY2026) to ~25bn in year 1 and ~40bn by year 10. The Vulcan ready-mix acquisition is excluded from both the flows and the net debt (its pre-funding cash is left in the bridge).
scenario_narratives.bull: Three consecutive years of domestic price revisions prove structural rather than cyclical: the domestic cement operating margin reaches management's 10%+ target, group EBITDA margin holds 16-16.5%. Energy and freight stay benign, CalPortland benefits from the LA Olympics build-out, Bay Area data-centre construction (now with the Vulcan ready-mix footprint) and reshoring. Growth capex normalises to ~8% of revenue once Medium-Term-Plan projects complete, lifting FCF conversion. Terminal cap 15x. The Palliser-driven CalPortland monetisation is a further upside not in these flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: A repeat of the FY2023 energy shock: coal, fuel and maritime freight spike on Middle East escalation while price pass-through lags a year, so EBITDA margin drops to ~12% in years 2-3 and only recovers to 13%. Domestic demand falls 5-6% a year and pricing cannot fully offset; US West Coast housing stays weak; the Philippines unit needs a further impairment; Japan's GX-ETS carbon pricing adds cost and the C2SP/CCUS programme keeps capex at 9-10% of revenue. With 2.6x ND/EBITDA the DCF equity value in this path sits at or near the zero floor -- the business survives on its asset base and A+/A credit, but owner cash flow does not cover the debt plus a positive equity value at a 7.5% rate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a levered cyclical whose last energy shock (FY2023) took reported FCF to -64bn and whose overseas units impaired in two consecutive years; the bear path is a repeat of observed history, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- sustained domestic pricing against a 5-6%/yr volume decline, benign energy, a US cycle upturn and a capex step-down. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF DCF on the organic business at a JPY cost of equity of 7.5%, with cyclicality in the scenario flows and weights rather than the rate. The result is far below both book value (P/B ~0.7) and the market price because the business earns ~5% on invested capital and has spent 6-11% of revenue on capex against ~7% D&A for a decade; owner FCF has averaged ~23bn/yr on a ~460bn market capitalisation with ~380bn of net debt ahead of equity. The market is pricing the asset base (land, quarries, CalPortland) and the Palliser activist thesis (CalPortland sale/IPO at ~444bn, non-core real estate disposals); that is a sum-of-parts re-rating case the DCF does not grant. Memo: at 13x terminal FCF the implied terminal EV/EBITDA is ~3.3x versus ~5.8x today -- the gap is the price of the re-rating thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex intensity: every 1pp of revenue (~9bn/yr) of permanent capex above the 8.5% terminal assumption is worth roughly 800-900 yen/share at the base cap multiple
Energy/coal and freight shock (FY2023 analogue) with lagging price pass-through; the bear path puts DCF equity at the zero floor

Vulcan ready-mix acquisition ($712M) closes after the Q1 balance-sheet date: the model keeps the pre-funding cash and excludes the target; if the assets were bought above DCF value the bridge is generous by the difference
Philippines / emerging-market impairments recurring (24.8bn FY2026, also FY2025)
GX-ETS carbon pricing from FY2026-27 on a process-emission-intensive product; CCUS (C2SP kiln) capex with unproven economics
Upside risk: Palliser Capital campaign forces a CalPortland sale or US IPO at a multiple the DCF does not assume; domestic pricing proves structural and margins hold 16%+
Cross-shareholding bridge (138bn) is at balance-sheet fair value; a Japanese equity drawdown or forced unwinding at a discount reduces it
